accepted.justification: The exact images have no fstab entries. Declared execution is UID1000, read-only root, CapEff=0 and NoNewPrivs=1; no privileged mount caller or product mount endpoint exists. This excludes the required privileged fstab mount, not the presence of the installed util-linux package.

No fstab X-mount configuration exists; product processes do not invoke mount helpers. UID1000 with all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges cannot gain the privileged post-hook authority. Re-evaluate if privileged mounts or fstab entries are added.

No product or startup command invokes nsenter. The deployment uses a private PID namespace, no host cgroup mount and UID1000 with no capabilities; a privileged host operator running nsenter is outside this container workflow. The required root-created descriptor is absent.

The inspected fstab is empty and read-only; no X-mount.subdir operation is supplied by the product. UID1000/CapEff0/NoNewPrivs1 prohibit the privileged mount operation. Kernel version alone is not used to dismiss this CVE.

No fstab bind-mount authorization or X-mount hooks exist in the inspected runtime. Product subprocesses are fixed Python/LibreOffice/PostgreSQL tools, never mount; all capabilities are dropped and privilege gains disabled.

The product does not expose curl CLI schemeless SFTP/SCP with --proto-default and SSH trust options. System curl7.88.1 is used during the image build, not by runtime input handlers. Actual LibreOffice linkage selects its bundled libcurl8.22.0, after upstream fixes8.20/8.21; the Next proxy uses Node fetch with an operator-configured destination.

The upload reader uses CPython bundled Expat2.8.3, newer than fixes2.7.2/2.7.4/2.8.1 for these three CVEs. System Expat2.5 is linked by LibreOffice/fontconfig, whose XML input is pinned templates and bundled fonts; untrusted XLSX is never passed to LibreOffice. User text is escaped into fixed template nodes.

The actual upload path now parses all OOXML XML/rels with a DOCTYPE-start rejection before the internal subset or attribute normalization. Six exact-image regressions cover the upstream shape,100000 attributes, UTF16/chunk boundaries, metadata/rels and valid workbooks. This removes the input precondition; native Expat remains unpatched. Pinned DOCX templates are not uploaded by users.

ELF inspection locates direct calls only in the optional GTK3 GUI plugins, not the headless libmergedlo entrypoint. No D-Bus socket/address/DISPLAY is configured and uploaded XML goes to openpyxl, not D-Bus introspection. The missing input channel, rather than GLib package absence, is the basis.

libmergedlo creates/reads GVariants for D-Bus proxy calls; there is no D-Bus peer in the declared container. GSettings/system metadata are immutable image files; the product has no raw GVariant or settings upload API. ELF imports of GVariant in libgio are retained in evidence, not denied. Reassess if a host bus or user settings directory is mounted.

Neither the LibreOffice plugins nor the inspected transitive dependencies import g_date_time_add_full. Product dates are strict calendar strings inserted as XML text, not GDateTime arithmetic programs; no user-controlled GLib date arithmetic operation is exposed.

No LibreOffice module imports g_regex_replace; libgio imports the literal variant, which does not interpret case-change replacement escapes. Product values are Unicode JSON/XML text; arbitrary raw-byte GLib regex programs are not accepted.

No inspected LibreOffice or transitive dependency imports g_io_channel_set_line_term. libgio line-reader presence is acknowledged, but the custom-terminator setter/input required by this CVE is not exposed by the product. File-content import is Python/openpyxl, not configurable GIO channels.

libgio imports the function, but applicable desktop/GSettings key files remain read-only image metadata. User uploads are private image/CSV/XLSX files and no XDG configuration, desktop file or arbitrary filesystem destination is accepted. This conditional exclusion becomes invalid if mutable user settings directories or desktop imports are introduced.

No D-Bus system socket, session address, DISPLAY or host D-Bus mount exists in the inspected headless runtime. User input cannot configure a D-Bus peer. LibreOffice g_bus/proxy imports are acknowledged, but the required attacker-controlled server channel is absent.

No LDAP authentication/server/client endpoint exists in DEMO. Database authentication is a fixed PostgreSQL connection; URLs and connection options are operator configuration, not submitted form fields. No user BER input is passed to OpenLDAP.

The actual XML bindings used by LibreOffice and lxml are2.14.6, outside the affected range. The separately installed system2.9.14 is not the renderer binding, and untrusted XLSX DTDs are rejected before lxml parsing.
The upstream libxml2 Python binding is absent (import probe and filesystem search); lxml is a different binding. In addition the upload path rejects DTDs before downstream XML parsing.

The primary patch identifies overflow in4*(namelen+plen+1). Untrusted XLSX is capped at30MiB expanded XML with DTD expansion rejected; that cannot supply the approximately1GiB length required for the multiplication overflow. Generated DOCX QName names come only from hash-pinned templates; form values become text nodes, not names.

The primary patch checks xmlStrlen returning0 for lengths above INT_MAX. The entire accepted XLSX expansion is30MiB and API JSON2MiB; generated relation URIs are fixed/local template resources. There is no arbitrary multi-gigabyte URI construction or external resource URL input.

All untrusted XLSX DTDs are rejected by xml_input.py. openpyxl/renderer do not request DTD validation; DOCX input is a pinned template and generated content has no attacker-controlled DTD. Merely parsing XML does not invoke this validation diagnostic.

No XPointer or XInclude evaluation is called by renderer/openpyxl. The XPath expressions in rendering are fixed literals, distinct from XPointer processing. XLSX values never become XPath/XPointer programs; DOCX relationships are pinned/local.

The primary patch checks >=INT_MAX output buffers. DOCX jobs render one bounded recipient against a pinned template; direct batch renderer caps100 and images remain separate ZIP binary parts. XLSX export serializes bounded scalar cells incrementally with openpyxl/xmlfile, not a multi-gigabyte scalar passed to a custom callback. No custom output callback API is exposed.

Neither openpyxl nor renderer calls XInclude processing or supplies a custom external resource loader. XML_PARSE_NONET is not the sole defense: the affected operation is absent from the supported input path, and DOCX resources are pinned/local.
